summary.title: LLVM Tutorial: Table of Contents
summary.one_liner: This is the table of contents for the LLVM "Kaleidoscope" tutorial, a 10-part guide to building a simple language frontend in C++ on top of LLVM.
keywords: how to write a compiler with llvm
takeaways: Kaleidoscope is a simple language used to show how to implement a language using LLVM components in C++.
The tutorial covers the lexer, parser and AST, then code generation to LLVM IR.
Later parts add JIT and optimizer support, control flow, user-defined operators, and mutable variables.
The final parts cover compiling to object code, adding debug information, and other LLVM tips.
The page also links to external tutorials on creating an LLVM backend for Cpu0 and implementing an LLVM integrated assembler.
summary.summary: This page is the table of contents for LLVM's Kaleidoscope tutorial, which shows how to implement a simple language using LLVM components in C++. It lists ten chapters, from the lexer and parser through IR code generation, JIT and optimizer support, language extensions, object code output, and debug information. It also links to two external resources: a Cpu0 LLVM backend tutorial and a guide to writing an LLVM integrated assembler. The page itself is an index, so the detail lives in the linked chapters.
